run.name: Columbus McKinnon Corporation
run.title: CP-OS host session (CMCO)
run.summary: Columbus McKinnon is a heavily indebted but liquid industrial manufacturer early in digesting a transformational acquisition. Credit quality depends on realising synergies and turning earnings into cash to cut debt; investor control adds monitoring risk. Launched through CP-OS as of 2026-11-05 on the retained context; the EDGAR registrant name in that context is COLUMBUS MCKINNON CORP.

leverage.basis: Total debt / EBITDA. Total debt 2,412,308 over Credit Agreement TTM Adjusted EBITDA 467,796 (pro forma, management reconciliation); net debt = total debt less cash 110,900. Company-reported ratio 4.9x. On company-reported Adjusted EBITDA with no pro forma (LTM 331,193) the same total debt gives 7.28x and net 6.95x.

coverage.basis: EBITDA / cash interest. Company-reported Adjusted EBITDA 181,373 over interest paid 45,630. Overstates the run rate: EBITDA includes approximately two months of Kito Crosby, but the new debt was outstanding only from late January and early February 2026 and the first notes coupon was paid August 1, 2026, so no notes coupon is in this figure.

cash.basis: Cash. Undrawn = revolver availability 421.080 (500.000 less borrowings 59.644 less letters of credit 19.276); no capacity under the AR securitization facility. Company-stated liquidity 531.980. Excludes unsecured uncommitted non-U.S. lines. Cash includes 108.440 held by foreign subsidiaries.

gaps: Host session: an agent answered every module from the pinned filings and CP-5 is its own review. No independent review has been made. Treat the analysis as candidate.
CP-2 main limitation: Executed credit and investor documents, customer concentration and ratings are not supplied, and the improvement in leverage rests largely on management's pro forma earnings.
CP-1 main limitation: Covenant levels, trigger and the lender-defined earnings build rest on summaries and management adjustments, not executed documents.
